title: Candy Corn Bag

drivers.name: Price increase (6%)
drivers.evidence: Price rose from $3.85 to $4.08. Past 25% discounts lifted sales x1.45 on average (noise-adjusted). A 6% increase likely reduces demand. No past 6% hike observed, so apply moderate negative.

drivers.name: TikTok trend
drivers.evidence: Product trending on TikTok. No past social media spike observed. Noise-adjusted estimate for untested driver is shrunk to x1.10. Use conservative uplift.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 10.3. A price increase to $4.08 (+6%) is not a promotion, so it likely reduces demand. Past 25% discounts (2025-09-29, 2025-10-20) lifted sales x2.15 on average, but noise-adjusted effect was only x1.45. The recent 10% off (2026-09-07) lifted sales x1.75, but the product is now at a higher price. The TikTok trend is untested; no past spike from social media. The week after a promotion (2026-10-05) saw only 3 units, suggesting weak carryover. No event or holiday. The uplift model suggests no effect, but this ignores the price increase and trend. The price hike likely reduces sales. The TikTok trend is speculative. Combine: a small negative from price, a weak positive from trend. Shrink toward 1.0 due to thin evidence. Final median slightly below baseline.

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 10.3 | 5%-95%: 0.0 - 23.5 | 10%-90%: 0.0 - 18.6

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-85% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
